extraAngles.prompt: the PRIMARY critics DIRECT, not via Wikipedia or student blogs: Drout, 'Tolkien's Prose Style and its Literary and Rhetorical Effects', Tolkien Studies 1 (2004) — Project MUSE abstract and Drout's own Wormtalk summaries; Raffel, 'The Lord of the Rings as Literature' (Tolkien and the Critics, 1968), Stimpson (1969) and Manlove, Modern Fantasy (1975) — Google Books snippet on 'not literature', 'wrenches syntax', 'overworked cadences'; Kirk, 'I Would Rather Have Written in Elvish', Novel 5.1 (1971) — Crossref/JSTOR first page; Bratman 2000 and Thomas, 'Some of Tolkien's Narrators' 2000 (Tolkien's Legendarium) — search-inside for 'Annalistic' and 'self-effacing' (three or four narrative modes?); Shippey direct (Author of the Century ch. 2: 'Elrondian', the Gaffer baseline; The Road to Middle-earth p. 203 'loose semantic fit') and Rosebury direct via Google Books snippet; Crabbe (1981/1988) and Mendlesohn, Rhetorics of Fantasy (2008) via archive.org _djvu.txt; Lobdell's full text at archive.org; Corey Olsen's Mythgard 'Exploring The Lord of the Rings' notes and Tolkien Professor transcripts on register at sentence level

TOLKIEN'S OWN THEORY of why a secondary world's language must hold: 'On Fairy-stories' (inner consistency of reality, sub-creation, Recovery, arresting strangeness), 'A Secret Vice' (phonaesthetics), 'Beowulf: The Monsters and the Critics' (the illusion of historical truth and perspective, the impression of depth), Letter 215 to Walter Allen (1959) on the children's-book manner he regretted, Letter 193 to Terence Tiller (1956) on Rohirric speech and delivery, Letter 210 on the film treatment ('miles are miles') — Wikipedia's essay pages, Tolkien Gateway (letters via the Wayback Machine as needed), tolkienestate.com; extract what the AUTHOR says the prose must do

THE CIVIC-RECORD TEXTS INSIDE TOLKIEN — the register nearest a settlement dossier: the Prologue's 'Of the Ordering of the Shire' (Shirriffs, the Thain, the Mayor, the Post), 'Concerning Pipe-weed', Appendix A's annals of kings and stewards, Appendix B's Tale of Years, the Red Book's found-manuscript frame, and Farmer Giles of Ham's mock-scholarly foreword and chronicle voice: how Tolkien writes institutions, offices, dates, customs and a village's history as RECORD rather than narrative — Wikipedia 'Farmer Giles of Ham' § Style, 'Shire (Middle-earth)' § Government, Tolkien Gateway 'Prologue', Halbrooks and Shippey on the antiquarian mode, any critic on the Appendices' annalistic prose

POINT OF VIEW, FOCALISATION and MEASURED SYNTAX: free indirect discourse and the hobbit-focalised narration (Kullmann & Siepmann's 'Points of View' and 'Narrative Syntax' chapters via Google Books search-inside id 9uAsEAAAQBAJ; Wikipedia 'Storytelling in The Lord of the Rings' § Points of view), sentence-length, clause-depth and punctuation FIGURES for Tolkien's prose (the Digital Tolkien Project at digitaltolkien.com, any stylometric or corpus study with numbers), and the 85-per-cent hobbit-viewpoint figure traced to its source

REGISTER AS A NATURAL EXPERIMENT: the German Krege (2000) retranslation that replaced Carroux's archaising register with colloquial German and was rejected by readers, the Swedish Ohlmarks case (Wikipedia 'Translating The Lord of the Rings' and de.wikipedia 'Der Herr der Ringe' § Übersetzungen); IMITATION FAILURE MODES — Bored of the Rings (1969) as a style parody, Diana Wynne Jones's Tough Guide to Fantasyland, the Sword of Shannara reception, Shippey's 'many imitators' passage in Author of the Century — what Tolkien-derived prose gets WRONG; and the 1981 BBC radio adaptation (Sibley and Bakewell) praised for keeping the dialogue register (Wikipedia § Reception, Sibley interviews)
